topic: Mechanical Advantage of Levers and Simple Machines
key_concepts: A lever has a fulcrum, resistance, and effort
Levers are classified by the relative positions of fulcrum, effort, and resistance
Effort force is the input force applied by the user
Resistance force is the output force exerted to overcome a load
Mechanical advantage is the ratio of output force to input force
Mechanical advantage can be calculated as resistance force divided by effort force
Mechanical advantage can also be calculated as effort arm divided by resistance arm
A mechanical advantage equal to 1 changes the direction of force
A mechanical advantage greater than 1 multiplies force
A mechanical advantage less than 1 increases speed
Pulley systems increase mechanical advantage as the number of pulleys increases
Wheel and axle mechanical advantage is the ratio of wheel radius to axle radius
